chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about game that a man strikes with a sword, or thrusts with a spear, or shoots with an arrow, so it kills it, and he had recited the name of God (Allahu Akbar) when he did that. He said: 'Eat it, there is no harm with it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for game killed by a weapon to be considered halal in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies that for game hunted with weapons, the recitation of God's name (Tasmiyah) at the moment of the strike or shot is sufficient to render the meat halal, even if the animal is not slaughtered in the traditional manner. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between hunting (sayd) and ritual slaughter (dhabihah), emphasizing the hunter's intent and invocation over the method of death. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the permissibility of various hunting tools in Islamic dietary law.
